indication: newly-diagnosed advanced high-grade serous/endometrioid ovarian cancer, post-platinum response
biomarker: all-comers (HRD-positive and HRD-negative strata; no BRCA mutation required)
inclusion_match_notes: PRIMA enrolled all-comers without requiring a BRCA mutation or a validated HRD score, which is the cleanest fit for this BRCA wild-type, genomically-unstable tumor. The patient matches on indication, 1L post-response timing, and ECOG. Thrombocytopenia and neutropenia are the dose-limiting toxicities and warrant the myelosuppression flag, partly mitigated by individualized (body-weight/platelet) starting dose.
intervention_dosing: oral niraparib 200-300 mg once daily (individualized starting dose)

indication: newly-diagnosed advanced high-grade serous ovarian cancer receiving 1L bevacizumab
biomarker: HRD-positive by Myriad MyChoice GIS >=42 or tumor BRCA mutation (benefit concentrated in HRD-positive)
design: randomized double-blind placebo-controlled, 1L maintenance added to bevacizumab
inclusion_match_notes: PAOLA-1 fits the indication, line, and the patient's existing bevacizumab backbone, but the predefined benefit requires HRD-positive status by a validated assay (MyChoice GIS >=42 or tumor BRCA). Altera's qualitative genomic-instability call does not satisfy that companion-diagnostic threshold, so fit is partial pending a validated GIS. Anti-angiogenic VTE and bleeding risk plus PARP-related myelosuppression both apply given the patient's high VTE history and prior IVC filter.
intervention_dosing: oral olaparib 300 mg BID + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV q3w

indication: newly-diagnosed advanced high-grade epithelial ovarian cancer, post-platinum response

Indication, line, and ECOG match. Anemia and neutropenia drive the myelosuppression flag; transaminase elevations are usually transient and the patient's baseline LFTs are normal.

indication: newly-diagnosed stage III-IV epithelial ovarian / primary peritoneal cancer
inclusion_match_notes: GOG-218 anchors the bevacizumab maintenance rationale the patient is already on, with a matched stage III-IV 1L indication and no biomarker gate. Anti-angiogenic class carries VTE, bleeding, and hypertension risk, which is relevant given the high VTE history and prior IVC filter, though none of the patient's named toxicity vetoes (neuropathy, myelosuppression) are triggered by bevacizumab itself.
intervention_dosing: bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV q3w with maintenance to 15 months

indication: newly-diagnosed epithelial ovarian / primary peritoneal cancer (high-risk subgroup benefit)

indication: ER-positive recurrent / maintenance high-grade serous ovarian cancer
inclusion_match_notes: The patient's ER-positive (~80% nuclei) status supports an aromatase-inhibitor option, and letrozole is oral and low-burden, which suits the stated preference and the 70-79 age band. Benefit is modest and tempered by PR-negativity, and the published evidence is single-arm rather than randomized, so fit is partial. No named toxicity veto applies; the main concern is arthralgia and bone-density loss on prolonged use.

indication: newly-diagnosed advanced epithelial ovarian cancer (neoadjuvant + interval debulking)
design: randomized phase 1/2 added to neoadjuvant carboplatin/paclitaxel (OVATION 2)
inclusion_match_notes: This is the regimen-matched program: the patient received GEN-1 (IMNN-001) with neoadjuvant carbo/paclitaxel and achieved R0, mirroring the OVATION 2 design. The IL-12 immunogene targets the tumor immune microenvironment rather than relying on the foreclosed MSI/TMB checkpoint axis, so the MSS/TMB-low status does not exclude it. No named toxicity veto is triggered; intraperitoneal delivery is generally well tolerated.
intervention_dosing: intraperitoneal GEN-1 (IMNN-001) 79-100 mg/m2 weekly with chemotherapy
